-- /home/altjoe/.config/nvim/lua/opencode-manage/skills.lua FINAL
-- opencode-manage.skills — skill metadata + lifecycle (doc 22, SL2).
-- Reads and WRITES the routing manifests:
--   global  : ~/.config/opencode/skills.policy.json
--   project : <project>/.opencode/skills.policy.json (nearest .opencode up
--             from cwd, stopping at the project root — same convention as
--             metrics.lua)
-- Merged view: project entries win by name.
--
-- Lifecycle is RE-TIERING first (doc 22 SL2): demote to `legacy` to retire a
-- skill, promote to `emergency` to hint it always — the skill file stays,
-- only the routing changes. Full removal (drop the manifest entry) exists as
-- the deliberate second step; SKILL.md files are NEVER deleted here. The
-- airlock rule holds: nothing is destroyed, every write is journaled.
--
-- Every write: journal snapshot + record, then the manifest is rewritten
-- pretty (2-space, sorted keys) with unknown fields preserved. A manifest
-- that exists but does not parse fails CLOSED for writes (never silently
-- overwritten) and open for reads.
--
-- PRETTY-JSON DUPLICATION: pretty_json below is a copy of registry.lua's
-- module-private helper. A shared json helper is the consolidation candidate
-- (to be recorded via registry_propose once this file is applied).

local journal = require("opencode-manage.journal")

local M = {}

M.TIERS = { "default", "conditional", "emergency", "explicit", "legacy" }

local function global_dir()
	return (vim.env.HOME or "") .. "/.config/opencode"
end

--- Pretty JSON, 2-space, sorted keys — the manifest is a hand-reviewed
--- artifact; never write it single-line. (Copy of registry.lua's helper.)
--- @param val any
--- @param indent number|nil
--- @return string
local function pretty_json(val, indent)
	indent = indent or 0
	local pad = string.rep("  ", indent)
	if type(val) == "table" then
		if vim.islist(val) then
			local parts = {}
			for _, v in ipairs(val) do
				parts[#parts + 1] = pad .. "  " .. pretty_json(v, indent + 1)
			end
			if #parts == 0 then
				return "[]"
			end
			return "[\n" .. table.concat(parts, ",\n") .. "\n" .. pad .. "]"
		end
		local keys = {}
		for k in pairs(val) do
			keys[#keys + 1] = k
		end
		table.sort(keys)
		local parts = {}
		for _, k in ipairs(keys) do
			parts[#parts + 1] = string.format("%s  %q: %s", pad, k, pretty_json(val[k], indent + 1))
		end
		if #parts == 0 then
			return "{}"
		end
		return "{\n" .. table.concat(parts, ",\n") .. "\n" .. pad .. "}"
	end
	if type(val) == "string" then
		return string.format("%q", val)
	end
	return tostring(val)
end

--- Nearest project .opencode dir: walk up from cwd; stop at the project root
--- (first dir with .git). No .opencode found -> nil (project scope absent).
--- @return string|nil
local function project_opencode()
	local dir = vim.fn.getcwd()
	for _ = 1, 12 do
		local candidate = dir .. "/.opencode"
		if vim.fn.isdirectory(candidate) == 1 then
			return candidate
		end
		if vim.fn.isdirectory(dir .. "/.git") == 1 then
			break
		end
		local parent = vim.fn.fnamemodify(dir, ":h")
		if parent == dir then
			break
		end
		dir = parent
	end
	return nil
end

--- The manifests in scope, global first (project wins on merge).
--- @return table[]  { scope = "global"|"project", file = string }
local function manifests()
	local out = { { scope = "global", file = global_dir() .. "/skills.policy.json" } }
	local pod = project_opencode()
	if pod then
		out[#out + 1] = { scope = "project", file = pod .. "/skills.policy.json" }
	end
	return out
end

--- Full decoded manifest. Absent/unreadable -> nil (no error). A valid table
--- without a `skills` table gets an empty one. Malformed -> nil + error so
--- writers fail closed (never overwrite what cannot be read).
--- @param file string
--- @return table|nil, string|nil
local function read_full(file)
	if vim.fn.filereadable(file) ~= 1 then
		return nil, nil
	end
	local f = io.open(file, "r")
	if not f then
		return nil, "cannot open " .. file
	end
	local raw = f:read("*a")
	f:close()
	if not raw or vim.trim(raw) == "" then
		return nil, nil
	end
	local ok, decoded = pcall(vim.json.decode, raw, { luanil = { object = true, array = true } })
	if not ok or type(decoded) ~= "table" then
		return nil, "does not parse: " .. file
	end
	if type(decoded.skills) ~= "table" then
		decoded.skills = {}
	end
	return decoded, nil
end

--- Build the viewer-facing record for one manifest entry.
--- @param name string
--- @param scope string
--- @param file string
--- @param e table
--- @return table
local function build(name, scope, file, e)
	local root
	if scope == "global" then
		root = global_dir() .. "/skills"
	else
		root = vim.fn.fnamemodify(file, ":h") .. "/skills"
	end
	local path = root .. "/" .. name .. "/SKILL.md"
	return {
		name = name,
		scope = scope,
		file = file,
		entry = e,
		tier = type(e.tier) == "string" and e.tier or "default",
		subject = type(e.subject) == "table" and e.subject or {},
		note = type(e.note) == "string" and e.note or nil,
		path = path,
		exists = vim.fn.filereadable(path) == 1,
	}
end

--- Locate one entry across scopes (project wins); carries the live manifest
--- data so updates write back to the scope that owns the entry.
--- @param name string
--- @return table|nil
local function find(name)
	local found = nil
	for _, m in ipairs(manifests()) do
		local data, err = read_full(m.file)
		if err then
			vim.notify("⚠️ skills manifest " .. err, vim.log.levels.WARN)
		end
		if data and type(data.skills[name]) == "table" then
			local rec = build(name, m.scope, m.file, data.skills[name])
			rec.data = data
			found = rec
		end
	end
	return found
end

--- Merged list: project entries win by name; sorted by name. Read-only —
--- malformed manifests are skipped with no notification (refresh-safe).
--- @return table[]
function M.list()
	local by_name = {}
	for _, m in ipairs(manifests()) do
		local data = read_full(m.file)
		if data then
			for name, e in pairs(data.skills) do
				if type(e) == "table" and type(name) == "string" then
					by_name[name] = build(name, m.scope, m.file, e)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	local out = {}
	for _, rec in pairs(by_name) do
		out[#out + 1] = rec
	end
	table.sort(out, function(a, b)
		return a.name < b.name
	end)
	return out
end

--- Apply a change to one entry: mutate the live manifest in memory, snapshot,
--- pretty-write, journal. Fails closed when the entry is missing or the
--- manifest cannot be read.
--- @param name string
--- @param op_name string  journal op label
--- @param reason string
--- @param mutate fun(entry: table, data: table)
--- @return boolean
local function update(name, op_name, reason, mutate)
	local rec = find(name)
	if not rec then
		vim.notify("❌ skills: no manifest entry for '" .. tostring(name) .. "'", vim.log.levels.WARN)
		return false
	end
	local data = rec.data
	local entry = data.skills[name]
	if type(entry) ~= "table" then
		vim.notify("❌ skills: entry vanished during update", vim.log.levels.WARN)
		return false
	end
	mutate(entry, data)
	local snap = journal.snapshot(rec.file)
	local lines = vim.split(pretty_json(data), "\n", { plain = true })
	if lines[#lines] == "" then
		table.remove(lines)
	end
	vim.fn.writefile(lines, rec.file)
	journal.record({
		ts = os.time() * 1000,
		path = rec.file,
		group = "skills",
		op = op_name,
		snapshot = snap,
		existed = snap ~= nil,
		reason = reason,
		sessionID = nil,
	})
	return true
end

--- Re-tier a skill (the primary lifecycle action — demotion over deletion).
--- @param name string
--- @param tier string  one of M.TIERS
--- @param note string|nil  nil = leave the note alone; "" = clear it
--- @return boolean
function M.set_tier(name, tier, note)
	if not vim.list_contains(M.TIERS, tier) then
		vim.notify("❌ skills: unknown tier '" .. tostring(tier) .. "'", vim.log.levels.WARN)
		return false
	end
	local label = "tier -> " .. tier .. (type(note) == "string" and note ~= "" and (" · " .. note) or "")
	return update(name, "skill-tier", label, function(entry)
		entry.tier = tier
		if type(note) == "string" then
			entry.note = note ~= "" and note or nil
		end
	end)
end

--- Set or clear the note (the WHY — "demoted: duplicates verbose-logging").
--- @param name string
--- @param note string  "" clears
--- @return boolean
function M.set_note(name, note)
	if type(note) ~= "string" then
		return false
	end
	return update(name, "skill-note", note == "" and "note cleared" or ("note: " .. note), function(entry)
		entry.note = note ~= "" and note or nil
	end)
end

--- Replace the routing subjects (the refs vocabulary; >=1 required).
--- @param name string
--- @param subjects string[]
--- @return boolean
function M.set_subjects(name, subjects)
	local cleaned = {}
	if type(subjects) == "table" then
		for _, s in ipairs(subjects) do
			if type(s) == "string" and vim.trim(s) ~= "" then
				cleaned[#cleaned + 1] = vim.trim(s)
			end
		end
	end
	if #cleaned == 0 then
		vim.notify("❌ skills: at least one subject is required — routing needs it", vim.log.levels.WARN)
		return false
	end
	return update(name, "skill-subjects", "subjects: " .. table.concat(cleaned, ", "), function(entry)
		entry.subject = cleaned
	end)
end

--- Drop the manifest entry — the deliberate full prune. The SKILL.md file is
--- kept: the skill simply stops being routed/hinted. Prefer demotion
--- (`legacy`) when the history matters.
--- @param name string
--- @return boolean
function M.drop(name)
	return update(name, "skill-drop", "entry dropped (file kept)", function(_, data)
		data.skills[name] = nil
	end)
end

return M

Read/write layer for the routing manifests (global + nearest project, merged; malformed manifests fail closed for writes) with lifecycle mutators — set_tier (re-tier first), set_note, set_subjects, drop (entry only; the file is never deleted). Every write journals a snapshot first; pretty JSON with sorted keys preserves unknown fields.

-- opencode-manage — the review console for the opencode manage plugin.
-- Proposal review + change journal + registry review + verdict store/viewer
-- + metrics interface + references + skills lifecycle.
-- Completely separate from opencode-ext (the chat viewer) — no overlap.
--
-- VIEWERS: proposals (<leader>ap / <leader>ac), journal (<leader>aj),
-- registry (<leader>ar), verdicts (<leader>av), metrics (<leader>at),
-- references (<leader>af), skills (<leader>ak) — all persistent two-pane
-- viewers with live previews, no bland pickers.
-- COMMANDS: :ManageMetrics (summary), :ManagePrune [note] (shaped prune),
-- :ManageIndex [root] / :ManageRef [path] / :ManageRefs /
-- :ManageRefPrune <id> <why> (references, doc 20).
-- Focus: BufEnter writes the active file so refs can route by what you work on.

local review = require("opencode-manage.review")
local reviewview = require("opencode-manage.reviewview")
local journalview = require("opencode-manage.journalview")
local registryview = require("opencode-manage.registryview")
local verdictview = require("opencode-manage.verdictview")
local metrics = require("opencode-manage.metrics")
local metricsview = require("opencode-manage.metricsview")
local refs = require("opencode-manage.refs")
local refsview = require("opencode-manage.refsview")
local skills = require("opencode-manage.skills")
local skillsview = require("opencode-manage.skillsview")

-- Keymaps
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>ap", reviewview.open, { desc = "Manage: review proposals" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>ac", reviewview.open, { desc = "Manage: review proposals (merged)" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>aj", journalview.open, { desc = "Manage: journal viewer" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>ar", registryview.open, { desc = "Manage: registry entries" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>av", verdictview.open, { desc = "Manage: verdict viewer" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>at", metricsview.open, { desc = "Manage: metrics viewer (turns + objects)" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>af", refsview.open, { desc = "Manage: references viewer" })
vim.keymap.set("n", "<leader>ak", skillsview.open, { desc = "Manage: skills lifecycle" })

-- Stable commands (path resolution lives in code, not in pasted one-liners)
vim.api.nvim_create_user_command("ManageMetrics", function()
	metrics.summary()
end, { desc = "Manage: metrics store summary" })

vim.api.nvim_create_user_command("ManagePrune", function(opts)
	metrics.request_prune(opts.args ~= "" and opts.args or nil)
end, { nargs = "*", desc = "Manage: request a shaped context prune (next opencode message)" })

vim.api.nvim_create_user_command("ManageIndex", function(opts)
	refs.index(opts.args ~= "" and opts.args or vim.fn.getcwd())
end, { nargs = "?", complete = "dir", desc = "Manage: index references under a root" })

vim.api.nvim_create_user_command("ManageRef", function(opts)
	local path = opts.args ~= "" and opts.args or vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0)
	if path == "" then
		vim.notify("❌ refs: no path given and the buffer has no file", vim.log.levels.WARN)
		return
	end
	refs.pin(path)
end, { nargs = "?", complete = "file", desc = "Manage: pin a reference" })

vim.api.nvim_create_user_command("ManageRefs", function()
	refs.summary()
end, { desc = "Manage: list references" })

vim.api.nvim_create_user_command("ManageRefPrune", function(opts)
	local id, reason = opts.args:match("^(%d+)%s+(.+)$")
	if not id then
		vim.notify("❌ usage: :ManageRefPrune <id> <reason>", vim.log.levels.WARN)
		return
	end
	refs.prune(tonumber(id), reason)
end, { nargs = "+", desc = "Manage: prune a reference, keeping the reason" })

-- R1: focus routing — write the active file so refs match what you work on.
vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("BufEnter", {
	callback = function()
		local buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
		if vim.bo[buf].buftype ~= "" then
			return
		end
		local name = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(buf)
		if name ~= "" then
			refs.request_focus(name)
		end
	end,
})

-- API surface for scripting / later integration
return {
	review = review,
	reviewview = reviewview,
	journalview = journalview,
	registryview = registryview,
	verdictview = verdictview,
	metrics = metrics,
	metricsview = metricsview,

}

# /home/altjoe/docs/opencode/manage-plugin/22-skills.md FINAL
---
title: 22 — Skills (SL1 + SL2)
status: active
links: [03-proposals, 10-skills-gating, 17-impact-registry, 18-staged-workflow, 19-context-metrics-and-removal, 20-references]
---

# Skills — emit, tier, route, retire

Status: **active** — SL1 applied (manifest, `emit_skill`, routing hint,
subject tags); SL2 (lifecycle viewer) emitted (group `skills-lifecycle`).
`manage-proposals` was the first skill through the pipeline.

Supersedes [10-skills-gating](10-skills-gating.md) (its disk-scan gating was
first reduced by doc 19 to capture plus optional validation). Picks up doc
18's S6 tier vocabulary — `default | conditional | emergency | explicit |
legacy` — as the routing contract, and doc 20's subject vocabulary as the
shared key between refs and skills.

## The problem

- Skills are files the user writes by hand. The AI can read them but cannot
  propose one; a procedure that proves repeatable has no reviewed intake.
- Nothing routes by what the user is working on: O1 captures skill loads as
  bare names (doc 19), so a load carries no subject and does not join the
  refs objects.
- No lifecycle: every skill is effectively tier-less, so routing would either
  hint everything or nothing; nothing records why a skill stopped surfacing.

## Contract

- **Bodies stay opencode-native.** Skills remain at
  `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (global) and
  `<project>/.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (project) — the `skill` tool
  keeps loading them unchanged; nothing here introduces a second loader.
- **Metadata lives in one manifest per scope**:
  `~/.config/opencode/skills.policy.json` (global) and
  `<project>/.opencode/skills.policy.json` (project), merged by name with
  project winning. Manifest over frontmatter: opencode owns the frontmatter
  (`name`, `description`); `tier`/`subject` change on a different cadence,
  and one diffable artifact beats rewriting 30 skill files per policy tweak.
- **The AI proposes, the user applies.** `emit_skill` queues two proposals in
  one group — the SKILL.md and the merged manifest — through the standard
  review queue (doc 03). Nothing is written until the user accepts.
- **Routing is a hint, not enforcement** — one `[skills]` line at most, same
  shape as `[refs]`. Loading stays the model's choice; whether it works is
  measured through `skill_load` events (doc 19), not asserted here.
- **Two reload domains.** opencode's skill registry is process-cached: a
  newly written or edited SKILL.md becomes *loadable by name* only after an
  opencode restart (the skill list is assembled at startup). The plugin's
  layer is always live — the manifest, the `[skills]` hint, the subject
  tags, and `ref_lookup` are read per call — and the hint carries each
  match's SKILL.md path, so a session whose registry is stale can read the
  body directly instead of waiting for a restart.

## Metadata schema

```json
{
  "skills": {
    "code-delivery": { "tier": "default", "subject": ["opencode-manage lua", "delivery"] },
    "batch-exec":     { "tier": "explicit", "subject": ["workflow"], "note": "explicit-only by design" }
  }
}
```

| Tier | Routing behavior |
|---|---|
| `default` | hinted when a subject token overlaps the focused file's derived subject |
| `conditional` | hinted only on an exact subject match (no token overlap) |
| `emergency` | hinted regardless of focus, ordered first (rare — e.g. ground-truth/realign) |
| `explicit` | never hinted; loaded only when the user or model names it |
| `legacy` | kept for history; never hinted |

`note` is optional free text: the WHY an entry sits at its tier.

Subjects share the refs vocabulary (doc 20): `deriveSubject` = directory token
+ extension (`opencode-manage lua`). Matching is token overlap with
extension tokens ignored on both sides; a skill whose subject is a single
extension token (`templ`, `lua`) matches that language's files deliberately.
Explainable, no model involved.

## `emit_skill` — the intake

Args: `name` (kebab slug), `description`, `content` (the body), `tier`,
`subject` (JSON array), `scope` (`global` | `project`, default global).

- The tool composes the SKILL.md frontmatter (`name`, `description`) from the
  args; `content` must be the body only — frontmatter in the body is a
  REQUIREMENTS error (one source of truth).
- Two proposals, one group `skill-<name>`: (1) `create` (or `replace` for an
  update) at the skill path, (2) `create`/`replace` of the manifest with the
  merged entry, pretty-printed. Both ride the existing viewer; no new viewer.
- Paths are tool-constructed under the declared skills root and slug-checked,
  so the emit-side parent-dir rule is relaxed for `create` here only (doc
  21's rule is unchanged for model-supplied paths; the nvim apply side
  already mkdirs parents for `create`).
- One manifest row is merged at emit time — emit one skill, apply it, then
  emit the next, so manifests merge front-to-back.
- Every validation error follows the doc 03 contract: what, why, how.

## Lifecycle (SL2) — re-tier first, prune last

A skill's life is adjusted through its ROUTING, not its file. The lifecycle
viewer (`<leader>ak`) edits the manifest entry; the SKILL.md stays where it
is — deleting skill files is never a viewer action.

| Action | Key | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Re-tier | `t` | `default` hints by subject · `conditional` exact subject only · `emergency` always · `explicit` never · `legacy` retire (kept for history) |
| Note | `n` | the WHY stored on the entry ("demoted — duplicates verbose-logging") |
| Subjects | `s` | edit the routing vocabulary (≥1 required — routing needs it) |
| Drop | `D` | remove the manifest entry: the deliberate full prune; the file stays, the skill simply stops being routed |
| Open | `o` | jump to the SKILL.md in your buffer |

- **Demotion, not deletion, is the default.** A skill that stops earning its
  hint is re-tiered — `legacy` keeps the audit trail, `explicit` keeps it
  loadable on demand. Only a skill that should not exist as a routing entry
  is dropped. This mirrors refs' prune-with-reason, except the reason here
  is the note plus the tier itself.
- Usage lives in the viewer: skill-tag touches and recent loads from this
  project's `event_tags` (cross-project usage stays a per-project view —
  honest limit).
- Every write snapshots the manifest into the journal first, so console
  edits are revertible like every other change.
- The viewer refuses to write a malformed manifest (never silently
  overwritten) and still lists entries from the other scope.

## Routing

- `focus` (R1a) → `deriveSubject(focus.path)` → `matchSkills`.
- One line, ≤3 entries, emergency first. Each match carries its SKILL.md
  path so a stale skill registry can be bypassed by reading the file:
  `[skills] focus=… — matched: code-delivery (default) → /home/…/skills/code-delivery/SKILL.md; load with the skill tool, or read the path directly when the skill list is stale.`
- `skill_load` events carry the skill name and its subjects as O1 tags, so
  objects mode (`<leader>at`, `t`) joins skill ⇄ subject, and `ref_lookup`
  on the same subject returns the user's own code — the two layers share one
  vocabulary.

## What this is not

- Not enforcement: no deny on skill loads; no auto-loading.
- Not a second loader: opencode still reads SKILL.md.
- Not a skill editor: the viewer edits routing metadata; SKILL.md stays
  opencode-native and is edited as a file.
- Not message-keyword tagging (doc 19 open question 3).

## Interface

- Tool: `emit_skill`.
- Files: `skills.policy.json` (global + project), SKILL.md under the skills
  roots.
- Hints: `[skills]` line (name · tier · path); O1 tags `skill` + `subject`.
- Lifecycle viewer: `<leader>ak` — `t` re-tier · `n` note · `s` subjects ·
  `D` drop entry (file kept) · `o` open · `r` refresh.
- No new nvim viewer for intake: skill proposals are ordinary proposals; the
  manifest is an ordinary file.

## Slices

| Slice | Content | State |
|---|---|---|
| **SL1** | manifest + `emit_skill` + `[skills]` hint + subject tags | applied (group skills-1; hint paths added in skills-hint-paths) |
| **SL2** | lifecycle: re-tiering (legacy retire / emergency promote), note, subjects, drop — the `<leader>ak` viewer + per-project usage | emitted (group skills-lifecycle) |

## Acceptance (verify live)

1. `emit_skill` a test skill → two pending rows, same group, in `<leader>ap`.
2. Accept both → `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` exists and the
   manifest carries the entry; the skill appears by name/description.
3. Load it (restart opencode first if the skill was just written — the
   native registry is process-cached) → a `skill_load` event with `skill` +
   `subject` tags is recorded; `<leader>at` objects mode shows both.
4. Open a file whose derived subject overlaps a declared subject → the next
   call carries the `[skills]` line (name · tier · path); `ref_lookup` on
   that subject returns the matching refs.
5. Fail-open: remove the manifest → no hint, no crash, skills still load.
6. Lifecycle: `<leader>ak` → `t` demotes a skill to `legacy` (manifest
   rewritten, journaled; the skill stops being hinted after the next call),
   `n` records the why, `D` drops the entry with the file intact.

## Open questions

1. Subject matching strictness — start at token overlap; tighten by outcomes
   (doc 19 C3).
2. Manifest provenance — reviewed proposals first; hand edits stay legitimate
   (it is the user's file).
3. Skill updates vs new names — `replace` on a name is an update; renaming is
   a new name + `legacy` on the old entry.

## Related

- [03-proposals](03-proposals.md), [10-skills-gating](10-skills-gating.md),
  [18-staged-workflow](18-staged-workflow.md) (S6),
  [19-context-metrics-and-removal](19-context-metrics-and-removal.md),
  [20-references](20-references.md).
reason: Doc 22 SL2: the lifecycle is re-tiering first and prune last (demotion keeps the audit; drop removes the routing entry and never the file), the <leader>ak viewer keys, usage from the project's event_tags, journaled manifest writes, the stale-manifest fail-closed rule, and the note field in the schema. SL2 marked emitted. Based on the on-disk doc (skills-hint-paths version).

-- opencode-manage.proposals — the review data.
-- Reads .ai-proposals/*.jsonl (written by the opencode manage plugin),
-- accepts (snapshot → write → record → status), rejects, and "deletes"
-- (snapshot → MOVE to <dir>/_old/ → record → status) proposals.
-- No files are ever permanently deleted — they go to _old/ next to them,
-- which is reversible and auditable.
-- The JSONL is ground truth: schema-valid tool-call args, never parsed prose.
-- T2 (10-verdict-capture.md): every accept/reject/move writes a verdict to
-- the shared SQLite store automatically — accepted | corrected (edited
-- before da) | rejected | moved_old. The correction diff is recoverable
-- from proposed_content vs applied_content.
-- PATH VALIDATION (doc 21): the apply side FAILS CLOSED. Only absolute
-- proposal paths apply; update ops (replace/edit_range/delete) require a
-- readable target and are refused otherwise; only create may mkdir parents.
-- A relative path is refused with a loud message — joining it to any root
-- is how web/web copies were born. The emit side enforces the same rules
-- (lib/proposals.ts validateProposalTarget).
-- DELIMITER GUARD: edit_range accepts on .ts/.tsx/.js/.lua files with grossly
-- unbalanced braces/parens warn with a confirm gate — an unbalanced apply can
-- break a file (or a plugin) at load. Heuristic: strings and comments can
-- false-positive, so it asks, never silently refuses (default is No).
-- Two per-proposal cwd predicates drive the viewer's 4-state filter:
--   _cwd       = the proposal's manifest dir is reachable from cwd
--                ("session in the cwd" — walk-up + glob-down discovery)
--   _cwd_file  = the AFFECTED FILE's absolute path is inside the cwd
-- Discovery scopes:
--   ALL      = cwd-reachable .ai-proposals + SCAN_ROOTS (project roots)
--   SESSION  = _cwd
--   FILES    = _cwd_file
--   NEITHER  = not _cwd and not _cwd_file (foreign session AND foreign file)
-- VISIBLE = pending + accepted (accepted rows stay in the viewer marked
-- [applied], so the review history is never a mystery).
-- All iteration is DETERMINISTIC (sorted dirs) — the item order never
-- reshuffles between refreshes.
-- Each proposal also carries _file/_line (in-place status updates) and
-- _project/_rel (display metadata).
-- MALFORMED-LINE GUARD: a jsonl line that decodes to a table without a
-- `path` field is SKIPPED (warned once per file), not fatal — one bad
-- line must never take the whole viewer down.

local journal = require("opencode-manage.journal")
local verdicts = require("opencode-manage.verdicts")

local M = {}

-- Roots scanned for the "all sessions" view. Each is globbed for
-- */.ai-proposals — one level deep, cheap at viewer open.
local SCAN_ROOTS = {
	vim.env.HOME .. "/projects",
	vim.env.HOME .. "/docs",
}

--- .ai-proposals dirs reachable from cwd: walk up 12 levels + glob down 2.
--- @return table<string, boolean> dir -> true
local function cwd_dirs()
	local dirs = {}
	local dir = vim.fn.getcwd()
	for _ = 1, 12 do
		local candidate = dir .. "/.ai-proposals"
		if vim.fn.isdirectory(candidate) == 1 then
			dirs[candidate] = true
		end
		local parent = vim.fn.fnamemodify(dir, ":h")
		if parent == dir then
			break
		end
		dir = parent
	end
	for _, d in ipairs(vim.fn.glob(vim.fn.getcwd() .. "/.ai-proposals", false, true)) do
		dirs[d] = true
	end
	for _, d in ipairs(vim.fn.glob(vim.fn.getcwd() .. "/*/.ai-proposals", false, true)) do
		dirs[d] = true
	end
	for _, d in ipairs(vim.fn.glob(vim.fn.getcwd() .. "/*/*/.ai-proposals", false, true)) do
		dirs[d] = true
	end
	return dirs
end

--- Every .ai-proposals dir: cwd-reachable plus SCAN_ROOTS. Value = whether
--- the dir is cwd-reachable (the SESSION predicate).
--- @return table<string, boolean>
local function all_dirs()
	local dirs = cwd_dirs()
	for _, root in ipairs(SCAN_ROOTS) do
		for _, d in ipairs(vim.fn.glob(root .. "/*/.ai-proposals", false, true)) do
			dirs[d] = dirs[d] or false
		end
	end
	return dirs
end

--- Read every proposal from every jsonl in every .ai-proposals dir.
--- Each proposal carries _file and _line so accept/reject can update in
--- place, plus filter/display metadata: _cwd, _cwd_file, _project, _rel.
--- Dirs are iterated SORTED — pairs() on a hash table is unspecified and
--- could reorder rows between refreshes (moving the viewer cursor).
--- Lines that decode to a table WITHOUT a usable `path` are skipped and
--- warned once per file — they are partial/corrupt emissions and must not
--- crash the viewer.
--- @return table[]
function M.list_all()
	local out = {}
	local cwd = vim.fn.getcwd()
	local dirs = all_dirs()
	local dir_list = {}
	for d in pairs(dirs) do
		dir_list[#dir_list + 1] = d
	end
	table.sort(dir_list)
	local warned = {}
	for _, dir in ipairs(dir_list) do
		local cwd_reachable = dirs[dir]
		local project_root = vim.fn.fnamemodify(dir, ":h")
		for _, f in ipairs(vim.fn.glob(dir .. "/*.jsonl", false, true)) do
			local lines = vim.fn.readfile(f)
			for li, line in ipairs(lines) do
				if line ~= "" then
					local ok, p = pcall(vim.json.decode, line)
					if ok and type(p) == "table" then
						if type(p.path) ~= "string" or p.path == "" then
							-- Malformed/partial line: warn once per file, skip
							if not warned[f] then
								warned[f] = true
								vim.notify(
									string.format("⚠️ Skipping malformed proposal line %d in %s (no path)", li, f),
									vim.log.levels.WARN
								)
							end
						else
							p._file = f
							p._line = li
							p._cwd = cwd_reachable
							p._project = vim.fn.fnamemodify(project_root, ":t")
							local abs = p.path
							if abs:sub(1, 1) ~= "/" then
								abs = project_root .. "/" .. abs
							end
							p._rel = abs:gsub("^" .. vim.pesc(project_root .. "/"), "")
							p._cwd_file = abs == cwd or abs:sub(1, #cwd + 1) == cwd .. "/"
							table.insert(out, p)
						end
					end
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return out
end

--- Apply a scope filter to a decoded proposal.
--- @param p table
--- @param mode string|nil  "all" | "session" | "files" | "neither"
--- @return boolean
local function in_scope(p, mode)
	if mode == "session" then
		return p._cwd
	elseif mode == "files" then
		return p._cwd_file
	elseif mode == "neither" then
		return not p._cwd and not p._cwd_file
	end
	return true
end

--- Proposals still waiting for a decision, in one of the four scopes.
--- @param mode string|nil  "all" | "session" | "files" | "neither" (nil = all)
--- @return table[]
function M.list_pending(mode)
	local out = {}
	for _, p in ipairs(M.list_all()) do
		if p.status == "pending" and in_scope(p, mode) then
			table.insert(out, p)
		end
	end
	return out
end

--- Visible proposals: pending + accepted (accepted stay in the viewer so
--- the review history is explicit — marked [applied] by row_state).
--- @param mode string|nil  scope filter (see in_scope)
--- @return table[]
function M.list_visible(mode)
	local out = {}
	for _, p in ipairs(M.list_all()) do
		local st = p.status or "pending"
		if (st == "pending" or st == "accepted") and in_scope(p, mode) then
			table.insert(out, p)
		end
	end
	return out
end

--- Resolve a proposal path to absolute, FAIL CLOSED (doc 21): only absolute
--- paths resolve. Relative paths return nil and every write path refuses
--- them with a visible message — joining it to any root is how the
--- web/web copies were born.
--- @param proposal table
--- @return string|nil
local function resolve_path(proposal)
	if type(proposal.path) == "string" and proposal.path:sub(1, 1) == "/" then
		return proposal.path
	end
	return nil
end

--- Refuse helper: visible, loud, never writes.
--- @param proposal table
--- @param action string
--- @return boolean  always false
local function refuse(proposal, action)
	vim.notify(
		string.format(
			"❌ Refused to %s: non-absolute proposal path (legacy entry):\n  %s\n  Re-emit with an absolute path.",
			action,
			tostring(proposal.path)
		),
		vim.log.levels.ERROR
	)
	return false
end

--- Update a proposal's status field in its jsonl (in place).
--- @param proposal table
--- @param status string  "accepted" | "rejected"
function M.set_status(proposal, status)
	if not proposal._file then
		return
	end
	local lines = vim.fn.readfile(proposal._file)
	local ok, obj = pcall(vim.json.decode, lines[proposal._line] or "")
	if ok and type(obj) == "table" then
		obj.status = status
		lines[proposal._line] = vim.json.encode(obj)
		vim.fn.writefile(lines, proposal._file)
	end
end

--- Accept a proposal: snapshot → write → journal → verdict → status flip.
--- The write is a USER-initiated action from nvim, never the AI.
--- Fail closed (doc 21): absolute path required; update ops require a
--- readable target; only create may mkdir parents.
--- T2: editing the buffer before accepting makes the verdict `corrected` —
--- the diff between INTENDED and applied content is the structural fact.
--- @param proposal table
--- @param content_override string|nil  use this instead of proposal.content
---   (the user may have edited the proposed content before accepting)
--- @param baseline_override string|nil  the full content the proposal intended
---   to produce. For edit_range this is the after-content, NOT the replacement
---   fragment — fragment-vs-file comparisons flagged every accept as corrected.
--- @return boolean  true when written
function M.accept(proposal, content_override, baseline_override)
	local path = resolve_path(proposal)
	if not path then
		return refuse(proposal, "accept")
	end
	local op = proposal.operation or "replace"
	local exists = vim.fn.filereadable(path) == 1
	if op == "create" then
		if exists then
			vim.notify(
				"❌ Refused: create target already exists:\n  " .. path .. "\n  Use replace/edit_range instead.",
				vim.log.levels.ERROR
			)
			return false
		end
		local parent = vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ":h")
		if vim.fn.isdirectory(parent) ~= 1 then
			vim.fn.mkdir(parent, "p")
		end
	else
		if not exists then
			vim.notify(
				"❌ Refused: "
					.. op
					.. " target is not readable:\n  "
					.. path
					.. "\n  Update ops never create files — re-emit as 'create' if that was intended.",
				vim.log.levels.ERROR
			)
			return false
		end
	end

	local snap = journal.snapshot(path)

	local content = content_override or proposal.content or ""
	-- Delimiter balance guard (doc 21 follow-up): an edit_range that leaves
	-- braces/parens unbalanced can kill a plugin at load — that is not
	-- hypothetical, it happened. Strings and comments can false-positive
	-- here, so this warns with a confirm gate instead of hard-blocking.
	if op == "edit_range" then
		local ext = vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ":e"):lower()
		if ext == "ts" or ext == "tsx" or ext == "js" or ext == "lua" then
			local depth = 0
			for ch in content:gmatch("[%{%(}%)]") do
				if ch == "{" or ch == "(" then
					depth = depth + 1
				else
					depth = depth - 1
				end
			end
			if depth ~= 0 then
				local choice = vim.fn.confirm(
					string.format(
						"⚠️ Delimiter balance is off (%+d) after this edit:\n  %s\n\nAn unbalanced apply can kill the plugin at load. Apply anyway?",
						depth,
						path
					),
					"&No\n&Yes",
					1
				)
				if choice ~= 2 then
					vim.notify("❌ Refused: unbalanced edit — review the range and re-emit", vim.log.levels.WARN)
					return false
				end
			end
		end
	end
	local lines = vim.split(content, "\n", { plain = true })
	if lines[#lines] == "" then
		table.remove(lines) -- writefile adds the trailing newline itself
	end
	vim.fn.writefile(lines, path)

	journal.record({
		ts = proposal.ts,
		path = path,
		group = proposal.group,
		op = proposal.operation,
		snapshot = snap,
		existed = snap ~= nil,
		reason = proposal.reason,
		sessionID = proposal.sessionID,
	})

	-- T2 verdict capture
	local verdict = "accepted"
	-- Trailing whitespace/newlines are not corrections, and edit_range
	-- baselines are full files — compare applied content against the intended
	-- baseline, normalized.
	local function norm_content(s)
		return (s or ""):gsub("%s+$", "")
	end
	local baseline = baseline_override or proposal.content
	if content_override and norm_content(content_override) ~= norm_content(baseline) then
		verdict = "corrected"
	end
	verdicts.record({
		ts = os.time() * 1000,
		session_id = proposal.sessionID,
		proposal_id = proposal.ts,
		group_name = proposal.group,
		path = path,
		operation = proposal.operation,
		verdict = verdict,
		reason = proposal.reason,
		proposed_content = baseline,
		applied_content = content,
	})
	verdicts.promote_if_cross_project(path, verdict)

	M.set_status(proposal, "accepted")
	vim.notify("✅ Accepted: " .. path, vim.log.levels.INFO)
	return true
end

--- Snapshot a file WITHOUT writing — the manual `y` path. Records a journal
--- entry so even copy-paste changes are revertible (the airlock covers
--- every way a file changes, not just `da`). Fails closed on relative paths.
--- @param proposal table
--- @return string|nil  snapshot path
function M.snapshot_only(proposal)
	local path = resolve_path(proposal)
	if not path then
		refuse(proposal, "snapshot")
		return nil
	end
	local snap = journal.snapshot(path)
	journal.record({
		ts = proposal.ts,
		path = path,
		group = proposal.group,
		op = "manual",
		snapshot = snap,
		existed = snap ~= nil,
		reason = "manual copy (y) — not yet written",
		sessionID = proposal.sessionID,
	})
	return snap
end

--- "Delete" a file: snapshot then MOVE it to <dir>/_old/<basename>.
--- Never permanently deletes — reversible and auditable.
--- The move is a USER-initiated action from nvim, never the AI.
--- Fails closed on relative paths.
--- @param proposal table
--- @return string|nil  the _old destination path, or nil if nothing moved
function M.move_to_old(proposal)
	local path = resolve_path(proposal)
	if not path then
		refuse(proposal, "move to _old")
		return nil
	end
	if vim.fn.filereadable(path) ~= 1 then
		vim.notify("ℹ️ File already gone: " .. path, vim.log.levels.INFO)
		M.set_status(proposal, "accepted")
		return nil
	end

	-- snapshot for reversibility
	local snap = journal.snapshot(path)

	-- destination: <dir>/_old/<basename>
	local parent = vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ":h")
	local old_dir = parent .. "/_old"
	local basename = vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ":t")
	vim.fn.mkdir(old_dir, "p")
	local dest = old_dir .. "/" .. basename
	if vim.fn.filereadable(dest) == 1 then
		-- avoid clobbering: suffix with a timestamp
		dest = old_dir .. "/" .. basename .. "." .. tostring(os.time())
	end

	local ok, err = vim.loop.fs_rename(path, dest)
	if not ok then
		vim.notify("❌ Move to _old failed: " .. tostring(err), vim.log.levels.ERROR)
		return nil
	end

	journal.record({
		ts = proposal.ts,
		path = path,
		group = proposal.group,
		op = "move",
		snapshot = snap,
		moved_to = dest,
		existed = true,
		reason = proposal.reason,
		sessionID = proposal.sessionID,
	})

	-- T2 verdict capture
	verdicts.record({
		ts = os.time() * 1000,
		session_id = proposal.sessionID,
		proposal_id = proposal.ts,
		group_name = proposal.group,
		path = path,
		operation = proposal.operation,
		verdict = "moved_old",
		reason = proposal.reason,
		proposed_content = proposal.content,
		applied_content = nil,
	})
	verdicts.promote_if_cross_project(path, "moved_old")

	M.set_status(proposal, "accepted")
	vim.notify("📦 Moved to _old: " .. path .. " → " .. dest, vim.log.levels.INFO)
	return dest
end

--- Reject a proposal: status flip + verdict. Nothing written. Rejection is
--- allowed for legacy relative rows too — it clears them from the queue.
--- @param proposal table
function M.reject(proposal)
	M.set_status(proposal, "rejected")

	-- T2 verdict capture
	local path = resolve_path(proposal) -- nil for legacy relative entries
	verdicts.record({
		ts = os.time() * 1000,
		session_id = proposal.sessionID,
		proposal_id = proposal.ts,
		group_name = proposal.group,
		path = path,
		operation = proposal.operation,
		verdict = "rejected",
		reason = proposal.reason,
		proposed_content = proposal.content,
		applied_content = nil,
	})
	if path then
		verdicts.promote_if_cross_project(path, "rejected")
	end

	vim.notify("❌ Rejected: " .. proposal.path, vim.log.levels.INFO)
end

return M

Only edit_range rows on .ts/.tsx/.js/.lua ask; default is No. Header documents it.

title: 23 — Permissions Manager (PM)
status: proposed
links: [11-nvim-companion, 20-references, 22-skills]

# Permissions Manager — remember folders, verify they applied

Status: proposed — design for review; nothing built.

Implements the intent-network folder-permissions design
(`../intent-network/02-permissions-tooling`) inside the manage console,
with one addition that matters: **verify** that remembered permissions are
actually in opencode's config, instead of assuming the write landed.

## The problem

- Every project re-asks for folders already trusted; opencode's
  `permission.external_directory` is hand-edited or forgotten.
- Approvals have no memory: what was approved lives in a config file
  nobody audits, and drift (hand-edit, typo, deleted entry) is invisible.
- The indexer and the capture offers walk into ignored trees
  (`node_modules`, build output), wasting attention.

## Contract

- **Memory vs enforcement.** state.db `folders` rows are the MEMORY;
  `opencode.json` `permission.external_directory` is the ENFORCEMENT
  surface. `s` sync writes the config (a console action, journaled,
  preserving every other key); `v` verify diffs memory against config and
  reports drift in both directions. No silent half-state.
- **Capture is free.** The plugin already tags every searched dir (O1 `dir`
  tags). The viewer offers those as candidates — approve once, never asked
  again.
- **Ignore files are respected, by git.** `git check-ignore --stdin` batch
  when the root is a repo (accurate, zero dependencies); `.ignore` +
  built-in patterns as the non-repo fallback. Ignored directories are never
  offered and never indexed.
- **Approval indexes.** Approving a folder runs the refs index over it and
  marks it `indexed`, so the folders you trust are also the folders the AI
  can cite your own code from (doc 20).

## Storage (state.db, additive)

| Table | Row | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| folders | one folder decision | id, ts, path, scope (project \| common), status (approved \| avoid), source (manual \| captured \| indexed), uses, last_seen, note |

`common` rows are the machine-wide trust set (the SCAN_ROOTS idea made
explicit: `~/projects`, `~/docs`, …); they apply in every project.

## Interface

- `<leader>aa` — the permissions viewer: approved / avoid / candidates
  (captured dirs not yet decided, ignore-filtered).
  `a` approve · `x` avoid · `d` remove · `o` open folder · `s` sync to
  opencode.json · `v` verify (drift report) · `r` refresh · `Q` close.
- Sync/verify target `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`
  `permission.external_directory` (currently a path array). Writes are
  journaled like every console action; the config is a hand-reviewed
  artifact — pretty JSON, other keys untouched.

## Restart semantics (verify live)

Whether a RUNNING opencode session picks up an `opencode.json` change is
unverified — until tested, sync reports: "written; restart opencode if the
running session still asks". `v` verify is the source of truth for the
FILE, not for process state.

## Slices

| Slice | Content | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| **PM1** | folders table + viewer + sync/verify | Quick |
| **PM2** | gitignore/.ignore respect in the indexer + capture offers | Short |
| **PM3** | approval → refs index + `indexed` marking | Quick |

## Honest limits

- nvim manages CONFIG and indexing — it cannot intercept opencode's read
  gate at runtime (that is opencode's own permission system).
- Captured candidates come from tool args (O1), so they show what the
  session touched, not everything under a root.
- `external_directory` is global config today; per-project scoping lives in
  our memory + generated globs (`~/projects/<x>/**`), not in opencode.

## Related

- `../intent-network/02-permissions-tooling` — the design this implements
- [20-references](20-references.md) — approval indexes refs; these ignore
  rules also govern the indexer
- [11-nvim-companion](11-nvim-companion.md) — the viewer family

# Secrets Redaction — present but masked

Status: proposed — design for review; nothing built.

The read gate denies `*.env` / keys to the AI, but secrets still reach the
context through tool output (a grep over a config file, git output, a pasted
line). This is the post-gate net: the plugin holds a dictionary of real
secret values and masks them wherever they appear in what the model reads —
with context, so a masking is visible, not silent.

## Contract

- **Plugin-side only.** env files are registered (never read by the AI); the
  plugin loads their values keyed by variable name. The dictionary never
  leaves the plugin.
- **Exact first, patterns second.** Registered values are matched
  byte-wise, longest first; pattern detection (password-like shapes) is the
  fallback for secrets that were never registered.
- **Contextual markers.** A secret is replaced by
  `[REDACTED:<LABEL> <prefix>…]` where LABEL is the env key or the pattern
  name, and the prefix preview is length-aware: 0 chars under 8, 2 chars
  8–19, 3 chars 20–39, 4 chars 40+. Surrounding text (the key, the line)
  stays — the reader sees THAT something was there and what kind.
  (User decision: label + short preview, both, scaled by secret length.)
- **Fail-open, never silent.** Redaction must never break a call; every
  redaction records a context event (kind `redact`, detail = label) so
  `<leader>at` shows what was masked.
- **Values under 8 chars are skipped** (false-positive control).

## Sources

- **Env registry**: explicit env-file paths/globs per scope — global
  (`~/.config/opencode/redaction.json`) and project
  (`.opencode/redaction.json`); managed by `:ManageEnv [path]` (add/list).
  The registry is user-owned; adding a file is a console action, never AI.

## Matching

1. **Dictionary**: registered values, longest first, exact substring.
2. **Patterns** (named, conservative): `password|passwd|pwd|secret|token|
   api[_-]?key|authorization` assignments; `Bearer …`; AWS `AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}`;
   GitHub `gh[pousr]_…` and `github_pat_…`; OpenAI `sk-…`; Anthropic
   `sk-ant-…`; Slack `xox[baprs]-…`; JWT `eyJ…`; PEM
   `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` blocks; URI credentials
   `://user:pass@`.

## Hook placement

| Hook | What it redacts |
|---|---|
| `tool.execute.after` | tool output before it returns to context |
| `experimental.chat.messages.transform` | message history before each model call (covers pasted/echoed values) |

Storage-side redaction (opencode's session JSONL / DB) is **out of reach**
for plugin hooks — this masks what the MODEL sees, not what opencode
stores. Recorded as an honest limit.

## Slices

| Slice | Content | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| **RX1** | env registry + dictionary + exact redaction + redact events | Short |
| **RX2** | pattern set + contextual markers (length-aware previews) | Short |
| **RX3** | management polish (`:ManageEnv` list/viewer) | Quick |

## Open questions

1. Entropy-based detection — defer; named patterns + dictionary first.
2. Per-provider pattern additions as encounters accumulate.
3. Whether verdict content (verdicts store) should also be redacted on
   write (currently: no — the store is local and user-owned).

## Related

- [19-context-metrics-and-removal](19-context-metrics-and-removal.md) —
  redact events live in the same metrics store
- [22-skills](22-skills.md) — same user-owned-artifact pattern
  (manifest + console-managed lifecycle)

# Manage — OpenCode Management Plugin

A modular opencode plugin acting as an **airlock between the AI and the
filesystem**, plus session/preferences/knowledge management. The user is the
only writer; the AI proposes, the user applies.

**The AI cannot touch your filesystem, ever. Its only output is structured
proposals. You are the only writer.**

# /home/altjoe/docs/opencode/manage-plugin/22-skills.md FINAL
---
title: 22 — Skills (SL1–SL3)
status: active
links: [03-proposals, 10-skills-gating, 17-impact-registry, 18-staged-workflow, 19-context-metrics-and-removal, 20-references]
---

# Skills — emit, tier, route, retire, load

Status: **active** — SL1 and SL2 applied (manifest, `emit_skill`, routing
hint, subject tags, lifecycle viewer). SL3 (the always-fresh loader)
emitted (group `skills-loader`). `manage-proposals` was the first skill
through the pipeline.

Supersedes [10-skills-gating](10-skills-gating.md) (its disk-scan gating was
first reduced by doc 19 to capture plus optional validation). Picks up doc
18's S6 tier vocabulary — `default | conditional | emergency | explicit |
legacy` — as the routing contract, and doc 20's subject vocabulary as the
shared key between refs and skills.

## The problem

- Skills are files the user writes by hand. The AI can read them but cannot
  propose one; a procedure that proves repeatable has no reviewed intake.
- Nothing routes by what the user is working on: O1 captures skill loads as
  bare names (doc 19), so a load carries no subject and does not join the
  refs objects.
- No lifecycle: every skill is effectively tier-less, so routing would either
  hint everything or nothing; nothing records why a skill stopped surfacing.

## Contract

- **Bodies stay opencode-native.** Skills remain at
  `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (global) and
  `<project>/.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (project) — the `skill` tool
  keeps loading them unchanged; nothing here introduces a second loader.
- **Metadata lives in one manifest per scope**:
  `~/.config/opencode/skills.policy.json` (global) and
  `<project>/.opencode/skills.policy.json` (project), merged by name with
  project winning. Manifest over frontmatter: opencode owns the frontmatter
  (`name`, `description`); `tier`/`subject` change on a different cadence,
  and one diffable artifact beats rewriting 30 skill files per policy tweak.
- **The AI proposes, the user applies.** `emit_skill` queues two proposals in
  one group — the SKILL.md and the merged manifest — through the standard
  review queue (doc 03). Nothing is written until the user accepts.
- **Routing is a hint, not enforcement** — one `[skills]` line at most, same
  shape as `[refs]`. Loading stays the model's choice; whether it works is
  measured through `skill_load` events (doc 19), not asserted here.
- **Three reload domains.** (1) opencode's native skill registry is
  process-cached: a newly written or edited SKILL.md becomes *loadable by
  name* only after an opencode restart. (2) The plugin's layer is always
  live — the manifest, the `[skills]` hint, the subject tags, and
  `ref_lookup` are read per call. (3) `skill_load` (manage, SL3) reads the
  manifest + SKILL.md directly, so a skill applied mid-session is usable
  immediately; the restart only refreshes the native tool. The hint carries
  each match's path and points at `skill_load`.

## Metadata schema

```json
{
  "skills": {
    "code-delivery": { "tier": "default", "subject": ["opencode-manage lua", "delivery"] },
    "batch-exec":     { "tier": "explicit", "subject": ["workflow"], "note": "explicit-only by design" }
  }
}
```

| Tier | Routing behavior |
|---|---|
| `default` | hinted when a subject token overlaps the focused file's derived subject |
| `conditional` | hinted only on an exact subject match (no token overlap) |
| `emergency` | hinted regardless of focus, ordered first (rare — e.g. ground-truth/realign) |
| `explicit` | never hinted; loaded only when the user or model names it |
| `legacy` | kept for history; never hinted |

`note` is optional free text: the WHY an entry sits at its tier.

Subjects share the refs vocabulary (doc 20): `deriveSubject` = directory token
+ extension (`opencode-manage lua`). Matching is token overlap with
extension tokens ignored on both sides; a skill whose subject is a single
extension token (`templ`, `lua`) matches that language's files deliberately.
Explainable, no model involved.

## `emit_skill` — the intake

Args: `name` (kebab slug), `description`, `content` (the body), `tier`,
`subject` (JSON array), `scope` (`global` | `project`, default global).

- The tool composes the SKILL.md frontmatter (`name`, `description`) from the
  args; `content` must be the body only — frontmatter in the body is a
  REQUIREMENTS error (one source of truth).
- Two proposals, one group `skill-<name>`: (1) `create` (or `replace` for an
  update) at the skill path, (2) `create`/`replace` of the manifest with the
  merged entry, pretty-printed. Both ride the existing viewer; no new viewer.
- Paths are tool-constructed under the declared skills root and slug-checked,
  so the emit-side parent-dir rule is relaxed for `create` here only (doc
  21's rule is unchanged for model-supplied paths; the nvim apply side
  already mkdirs parents for `create`).
- One manifest row is merged at emit time — emit one skill, apply it, then
  emit the next, so manifests merge front-to-back.
- Every validation error follows the doc 03 contract: what, why, how.

## `skill_load` — the always-fresh reader (SL3)

- `skill_load(name)` resolves the merged manifest, reads the SKILL.md, and
  returns the content + tier/subjects/scope/path. It bypasses opencode's
  process cache entirely — a skill applied mid-session loads without a
  restart. Called with an empty name it lists the governed skills (names,
  tiers, subjects, whether the file exists).
- Loads are recorded as `skill_load` events with subject tags (objects mode).
- Unknown names return the available list and the corrective action — the
  doc 03 contract, not a bare failure.
- The native skill tool remains the default once the registry has caught up;
  `skill_load` is the fallback that removes the restart requirement.

## Lifecycle (SL2) — re-tier first, prune last

A skill's life is adjusted through its ROUTING, not its file. The lifecycle
viewer (`<leader>ak`) edits the manifest entry; the SKILL.md stays where it
is — deleting skill files is never a viewer action.

| Action | Key | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Re-tier | `t` | `default` hints by subject · `conditional` exact subject only · `emergency` always · `explicit` never · `legacy` retire (kept for history) |
| Note | `n` | the WHY stored on the entry ("demoted — duplicates verbose-logging") |
| Subjects | `s` | edit the routing vocabulary (≥1 required — routing needs it) |
| Drop | `D` | remove the manifest entry: the deliberate full prune; the file stays, the skill simply stops being routed |
| Open | `o` | jump to the SKILL.md in your buffer |

- **Demotion, not deletion, is the default.** A skill that stops earning its
  hint is re-tiered — `legacy` keeps the audit trail, `explicit` keeps it
  loadable on demand. Only a skill that should not exist as a routing entry
  is dropped. This mirrors refs' prune-with-reason, except the reason here
  is the note plus the tier itself.
- Usage lives in the viewer: skill-tag touches and recent loads from this
  project's `event_tags` (cross-project usage stays a per-project view —
  honest limit).
- Every write snapshots the manifest into the journal first, so console
  edits are revertible like every other change.
- The viewer refuses to write a malformed manifest (never silently
  overwritten) and still lists entries from the other scope.

## Routing

- `focus` (R1a) → `deriveSubject(focus.path)` → `matchSkills`.
- One line, ≤3 entries, emergency first. Each match carries its SKILL.md
  path:
  `[skills] focus=… — matched: code-delivery (default) → /home/…/skills/code-delivery/SKILL.md; load with skill_load (always fresh) or the skill tool when the registry has it.`
- `skill_load` events carry the skill name and its subjects as O1 tags, so
  objects mode (`<leader>at`, `t`) joins skill ⇄ subject, and `ref_lookup`
  on the same subject returns the user's own code — the two layers share one
  vocabulary.

## What this is not

- Not enforcement: no deny on skill loads; no auto-loading.
- Not a second loader: opencode still reads SKILL.md; `skill_load` reads the
  same file on demand.
- Not a skill editor: the viewer edits routing metadata; SKILL.md stays
  opencode-native and is edited as a file.
- Not message-keyword tagging (doc 19 open question 3).

## Interface

- Tools: `emit_skill` (intake), `skill_load` (always-fresh reader; no name =
  list).
- Files: `skills.policy.json` (global + project), SKILL.md under the skills
  roots.
- Hints: `[skills]` line (name · tier · path); O1 tags `skill` + `subject`.
- Lifecycle viewer: `<leader>ak` — `t` re-tier · `n` note · `s` subjects ·
  `D` drop entry (file kept) · `o` open · `r` refresh.
- No new nvim viewer for intake: skill proposals are ordinary proposals; the
  manifest is an ordinary file.

## Slices

| Slice | Content | State |
|---|---|---|
| **SL1** | manifest + `emit_skill` + `[skills]` hint + subject tags | applied (group skills-1; hint paths added in skills-hint-paths) |
| **SL2** | lifecycle: re-tiering (legacy retire / emergency promote), note, subjects, drop — the `<leader>ak` viewer + per-project usage | applied (group skills-lifecycle) |
| **SL3** | `skill_load` — the always-fresh reader (no restart for applied skills) | emitted (group skills-loader) |

## Acceptance (verify live)

1. `emit_skill` a test skill → two pending rows, same group, in `<leader>ap`.
2. Accept both → `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` exists and the
   manifest carries the entry; the skill appears by name/description.
3. Load it — via `skill_load` immediately (no restart), or the native skill
   tool after an opencode restart → a `skill_load` event with `skill` +
   `subject` tags is recorded; `<leader>at` objects mode shows both.
4. Open a file whose derived subject overlaps a declared subject → the next
   call carries the `[skills]` line (name · tier · path); `ref_lookup` on
   that subject returns the matching refs.
5. Fail-open: remove the manifest → no hint, no crash, skills still load.
6. Lifecycle: `<leader>ak` → `t` demotes a skill to `legacy` (manifest
   rewritten, journaled; the skill stops being hinted after the next call),
   `n` records the why, `D` drops the entry with the file intact.

## Open questions

1. Subject matching strictness — start at token overlap; tighten by outcomes
   (doc 19 C3).
2. Manifest provenance — reviewed proposals first; hand edits stay legitimate
   (it is the user's file).
3. Skill updates vs new names — `replace` on a name is an update; renaming is
   a new name + `legacy` on the old entry.

## Related

- [03-proposals](03-proposals.md), [10-skills-gating](10-skills-gating.md),
  [18-staged-workflow](18-staged-workflow.md) (S6),
  [19-context-metrics-and-removal](19-context-metrics-and-removal.md),
  [20-references](20-references.md).

# /home/altjoe/docs/opencode/manage-plugin/19-context-metrics-and-removal.md FINAL
---
title: 19 — Context Metrics and Removal (C1–C4, O1)
status: active
links: [03-proposals, 10-skills-gating, 11-nvim-companion, 18-staged-workflow]
---

# Context Metrics and Removal — measure, remove, evaluate, objectify

Status: **active** — C1, C2 and O1 are built; C4 (selective reclamation)
emitted (group `context-reclamation`); C3 (retention stats + the measured
automatic trigger) is next.

Implements the intent-network measurement family (../intent-network/04-sidecar,
05-evaluation-layer, 08-context-mechanisms) inside the manage plugin +
state.db. Supersedes doc 18's S4 (the compacting half is C2) and S6 (skill
tiers — reduced to machine tags), and doc 10 (skills gating — reduced to
capture plus optional validation). Wording/injection is deliberately not the
mechanism: intent is measured, not prompted.

## As built

| Piece | State |
|---|---|
| C1 capture (turn_metrics, context_events) | live — verified: 32+ turns, 44+ tool calls recorded in one session store |
| C1 read (`:ManageMetrics`, `metrics.turns/events`) | live — colon-call driver fix required first |
| C2 prune request + shaped compaction | live — cache_read resets after compactions (448k→354k, 479k→285k) while input spikes show the summarizer at work |
| C2 interface (`<leader>at`, `:ManagePrune`) | live — turn badges + cache deltas make prune effects visible |
| O1 objects/tags (event_tags, objects mode) | built — files, dirs, patterns, symbols, skills, groups captured from tool args; viewer `t` toggles turns ⇄ objects; per-file verdict outcomes |
| C4 selective reclamation (messages.transform) | emitted — measured need below |
| Verdict integrity (false `corrected` fixes) | live — normalized baseline comparisons; injection carries reasons (accepted) and changed lines (corrected) |

Three driver bugs died on the way, all silent: lsqlite3-style API calls that
kkharji/sqlite.lua does not have; `sqlite.open(path)` (dot-call, no self)
falling back to an in-memory DB; and plugin-side `node:sqlite` not existing
under Bun (runtime-adaptive loader now picks `bun:sqlite` or `node:sqlite`).

## The problem

Context only grows. Every turn adds tool output, dead ends, superseded code,
and plan text; nothing removes any of it. Removal must be structural and its
effect measurable, or it is theater.

## Architecture

```
session events ──► manage.ts hooks ──► state.db (turn_metrics, context_events,
                                              event_tags, verdicts)
                                              │
                    nvim console ◄────────────┤  :ManageMetrics · <leader>at
                                              │
nvim :ManagePrune ──► prune_request row ──► plugin claims on next message
                                              │
                     experimental.session.compacting shapes ──► client.session.summarize

messages.transform ──► C4 reclamation: stale tool payloads stubbed
                       (old completed parts only; recent window untouched)
```

- Capture is plugin-only (event + tool hooks). No new process.
- Storage is the existing `state.db` (project + global), additive tables.
- Removal reads metrics + verdicts; it never asks the model to decide.

## C1 — Measure (built)

| Table | Row per | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| turn_metrics | assistant message (upsert by message_id) | session_id, message_id, ts, tokens_input/output/reasoning, cache_read/write, model, agent |
| context_events | notable act | session_id, ts, kind (tool_call / skill_load / proposal / registry_proposal / prune_request / prune_consumed / skill_proposal / evict / compaction), detail, subject |
| event_tags (O1) | object on an event | event_ts, session_id, tag, kind (file / dir / pattern / symbol / skill / group) |

Capture points: `message.updated` (assistant usage), `tool.execute.after`
(tool calls + object tags), `tool.execute.before` on `skill`, proposal and
registry emits, prune request/consume, C4 evict passes, `session.compacted`.
Aggregation views: `v_session_growth`, `v_tool_usage`, `v_object_usage`.

## C2 — Remove (built, coarse)

1. In nvim: `:ManagePrune [note]` — writes one `prune_request` event.
2. On the next user message the plugin claims it (`prune_consumed` row +
   in-memory flag).
3. `experimental.session.compacting` shapes that compaction: keep verified
   state, accepted/rejected outcomes, decisions, paths, open questions, the
   current task; drop exploration, superseded code and plans, tool noise.
4. `client.session.summarize({ path: { id } })` triggers the compaction. On
   failure the request is kept and retried next message.

Acceptance (proven): `cache_read` resets after a prune; the summarizer shows
as a large `tokens_input` spike; both visible per turn in the viewer.

Honest limit: whole-session compaction with keep/drop instructions — coarse.
**C4 is the finer pass** (below): it reclaims what compaction kept.

## C4 — Selective reclamation (emitted)

Measured on a live long session (2026-09-14, this project): a ~510k-token
prompt was ~70% stale tool output — **40 `read` results ≈ 1.44MB** — plus
**24 proposal payloads ≈ 383KB**; reasoning was 784KB in storage but is not
re-sent. Whole-session compaction never shrank it durably: within minutes
the prompt climbed back to ~500k. The dead weight lives in history, not in
the summary.

C4 evicts at the message level: in `messages.transform` (the removal
channel), old **completed** tool parts are stubbed —

- `read`/`grep`/`glob` outputs over a size threshold →
  `[evicted: read /path — output reclaimed by manage (C4); re-read if
  needed]`
- proposal/registry/skill-call payloads (`state.input.content` over
  threshold) →
  `[evicted: emit_proposal payload for /path — reviewed/applied; the file
  on disk and the journal are the truth]`

Rules: the most recent messages are never touched (keep-window of 6); only
parts with `status: completed`; stubs are idempotent (`[evicted:` prefix);
the part stays in place so call/result pairing is preserved; every pass with
work records one `evict` event (parts, KB) and the effect is visible as a
`cache_read` drop in `<leader>at`. Reasoning parts are never touched
(provider signature/continuity semantics).

Acceptance: on a session with stale bulk, the first call after applying C4
shows a `cache_read` drop of roughly the measured evicted volume; the AI can
re-read/re-run anything it still needs; `evict` events appear in the viewer.

## O1 — Objects / tags (built)

Mechanical named-object recognition, no model involved:

- **Tool args** → tags: `read`/LSP `filePath` → `file`; `grep`/`glob` `path` →
  `dir` and `pattern` → `pattern`; `lsp_symbols.query` → `symbol`; `skill.name`
  → `skill`; proposal `path`/`group` → `file`/`group`.
- **Storage**: `event_tags(event_ts, session_id, tag, kind)` — joined to
  events by timestamp.
- **Aggregates**: touches + last seen per object; for `file` objects, verdict
  outcomes joined by absolute path (accepted / corrected / rejected counts).
- **Interface**: `<leader>at`, press `t` — objects list (kind · touches · last
  seen · tag), detail shows the verdict breakdown and the recent events under
  that tag.

Caveats: tags are exact strings from tool args (absolute paths match
verdicts; relative paths may not); `pattern` tags are noisy by nature and are
candidates, not truth. Message-keyword extraction is deliberately deferred.

## C3 — Evaluate (pending)

Derived stats from verdicts + turn_metrics + event_tags (SQL, no model):
per-object acceptance/correction rates and recency feed retention tiers
(intent-network 08 section 3): frequent + accepted = keep; single-occurrence
+ corrected = prune candidate. Explainable stats only; mechanism
promotion/demotion (05) later.

C3's stats are also the natural input for (a) C4's eviction priorities
(what may be reclaimed first) and (b) the automatic prune trigger.

## Interface

- `<leader>at` — metrics viewer, two modes (`t` toggles):
  turns (time · in · out · cache · delta · badge) and objects
  (kind · touches · last seen · tag). `j/k`, `r`, `Q`.
- `:ManageMetrics` — one-shot summary (`:messages`).
- `:ManagePrune [note]` — request a prune.
- Errors surface in `:messages`; there is no silent fail-open in the nvim store.

## Honest limits

- Token metrics depend on provider usage fields; absent fields are skipped.
- Removal is structural first: verified slices, verdict history, recency.
- Object tags come from tool arguments — the AI's own words are not tagged
  (deferred: message keyword candidates, review-gated).
- C4 rules are size + age heuristics, not judgments of relevance; the
  keep-window is the protection, and everything evicted is recoverable by
  re-reading or re-running.
- Continuous verdict capture with origin weights (every user message, not
  just proposal completions) remains the intent-network verdict docs' job
  (10/11).

## Slices

| Slice | Content | State |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** | metrics capture + read interface | done |
| **C2** | prune request + shaped compaction | done (coarse) |
| **O1** | objects/tags + objects mode | done |
| **C4** | selective reclamation of stale tool payloads at the message boundary | emitted |
| **C3** | verdict-derived stats + retention candidates + measured automatic trigger | next |

## Open questions

1. Prune trigger: manual only until C4's reclamation is measured; then C3
   stats + a token threshold (with hysteresis) can request the prune.
2. Protected window for C3-driven eviction priorities (C4 keeps 6 messages;
   C3 can rank what goes first).
3. Message-keyword tagging: adopt (review-gated) or keep tool-args-only.

## Related

- ../intent-network/04-sidecar, 05-evaluation-layer, 08-context-mechanisms
- [18-staged-workflow](18-staged-workflow.md) — S4 implemented here as C2
- [10-skills-gating](10-skills-gating.md) — reduced to tags + validation
- [11-nvim-companion](11-nvim-companion.md) — the viewer family
reason: Doc 19 C4: selective reclamation — the measured breakdown (1.44MB reads, 383KB proposal payloads, 510k prompt), the message-boundary eviction rules (old completed parts, keep-window 6, labeled stubs, pairing preserved, evict events), C4 slice row, compaction visibility in C1's capture list, and the honest limits updated (C4 is the finer pass C2 left open).

# Manage — OpenCode Management Plugin

A modular opencode plugin acting as an **airlock between the AI and the
filesystem**, plus session/preferences/knowledge management. The user is the
only writer; the AI proposes, the user applies.

## The one-sentence contract

**The AI cannot touch your filesystem, ever. Its only output is structured
proposals. You are the only writer.**

## Document map

| [06-preferences](06-preferences.md) | Auto-inject your preferences every session |

| ~~[10-skills-gating](10-skills-gating.md)~~ | Superseded by [22-skills](22-skills.md) |
| [11-nvim-companion](11-nvim-companion.md) | The review console: diffs, journal, picker |
| [12-hooks-stability](12-hooks-stability.md) | Which hooks, and how stable they are |

| [14-build-order](14-build-order.md) | Milestones with a kill switch |
| [15-open-questions](15-open-questions.md) | Decisions still to make |

# Handoff - UI layout contract (panels/targets/OOB) + emit-time validation

## Goal
Give the AI one machine-readable source of truth for per-project UI layout and
htmx wiring, and enforce it at the emit_proposal airlock so panel/class/OOB
drift cannot be proposed. The AI keeps shipping htmx wiring that was "known"
in prose (docs/14, skills htmx-conventions / templ-ui) but is not
machine-checkable, so consistency depends on recall - which fails.

## Instructions
- Full-file proposals only, through emit_proposal; never edit files directly.
- Scope: ~/.config/opencode/plugins/* (manage.ts, lib/*),
  ~/.config/nvim/lua/opencode-manage/*, and the docs herein.
- Contract data lives per project: <project>/.opencode/manage.ui.json; grow it
  through a reviewed channel (same console flow as registry_propose, <leader>ar).
- Do not touch the volleyball-new tree from this session; the volleyball
  session owns the defect fixes.
- Verify with a real emit against a contracted project; reasoning alone is not
  evidence.

## Evidence (verified 2026-09-14, volleyball-new players workspace)
1. Templ boolean-attribute bug: `selected={ bool }` generated
   `selected="false"`; the attribute still selects, so every option was
   selected -> phantom filters were sent -> empty lists. Fixed in
   page.templ FINAL-22; a static check would have caught it before queueing.
2. Vertical/horizontal layout tabs render only in the full-page header and are
   absent from PlayerWorkspaceTabsOOB: after browse->compare they linger (and
   still target #tab-content, so games content lands inside the compare
   panel); after compare->browse they never appear.
3. BrowseLayoutResponse renders only the #tab-content content; no OOB for
   #browse-layout-tabs, so the active underline never moves.
4. View-switch class drift: only #detail-content innerHTML swaps; the shell
   never re-renders. #list-panel keeps its 50%/70% class variant,
   #detail-content keeps fill-vs-tabbed scroll mode, #tab-content keeps the
   wrong scroll class, and the browse divider is missing after switching from
   compare.
5. #detail-content receives three different fragments (browse header, compare
   center, panel header) with no declared binding for which may render there.
6. No hx-sync / hx-indicator / hx-push-url anywhere in the tree; the #skeleton
   fade CSS is dead (nothing targets it). Swaps give no loading feedback and
   rapid clicks interleave responses into the same targets.

Files: /home/altjoe/projects/volleyball-new/web/ui/html/players/page.templ,
web/internal/handlers/players/players.go,
web/ui/html/layouts/skeleton.templ, web/ui/html/layouts/player.templ,
web/ui/static/css/output.css.

## Required behavior
- R1 Contract (per project, reviewed): pages -> views -> panels
  {id, class variant per view, width ratio, scroll mode}; swap targets
  {id -> allowed fragment components}; actions {trigger -> route -> target ->
  swap -> OOB ids[]}; view-conditional fragments {component -> owner region ->
  the OOB that keeps it fresh}.
- R2 Manifest tool: `layout_manifest(page, view)` returns the composed layout
  tree plus an ASCII sketch from contract + templ/handler sources; optional
  drift check against a fetched URL (declared vs served DOM).
- R3 Emit-time validation: emit_proposal touching *.templ / handler files in a
  contracted project runs these checks and fails with REQUIREMENTS (append
  nothing):
  a) templ boolean attributes must use `?=` (flag `attr={ bool }` for
     selected/checked/disabled).
  b) every hx-target id exists in the contract; swap style matches the
     contract entry.
  c) every view-conditional fragment is in the OOB set of every response that
     changes its owning region.
  d) a response component's declared render target matches the caller's
     hx-target (no target/fragment mismatches).
  e) shell elements (panel classes, ratios, scroll modes, dividers) change
     only through a shell swap or explicit OOB - never left to innerHTML
     content swaps.
- R4 Components x request methods matrix as contract data + skill text: for
  each gencomponent (Common/Hx/FormBehavior/Keymap/Close) x method (GET nav,
  GET partial, POST form, POST->poll, SSE): allowed hx-* set, required
  companions, forbidden combos.
- R5 No custom LSP in slice 1. The R3 checker core is the reusable asset; a
  thin LSP adapter (or an lsp_diagnostics wrapper) is a later slice if editor
  squiggles are wanted. A per-project LSP would duplicate templ's own syntax
  LSP and add little beyond the emit-time gate.

## As built (LC1 + LC3) — emitted group `ui-layout-contract`

- **LC1**: contract at `<project>/.opencode/manage.ui.json` (nearest
  `.opencode` up from the proposed file; a `.git` boundary ends the walk).
  The reviewed write channel is `emit_proposal` itself: the contract is a
  single JSON document, so it rides as a full-file create/replace through the
  standard console — same queue, journal, and group revert; no second pending
  file to drift. When the target IS `manage.ui.json`, the plugin validates
  the shape first (panel ids, action targets, typed arrays) and refuses
  malformed contracts with a REQUIREMENTS error — nothing queues.
- **LC3**: `emit_proposal` on `*.templ` (always) or `*.go` files carrying
  htmx wiring (`hx-`/`templ.`) in a contracted project runs the R3 checks
  before queueing: (a) boolean attrs, (b) hx-target ids + declared swap,
  (c) view-conditional OOB coverage, (d) component target agreement, and
  (e) declared actions for shell targets. Violations throw a REQUIREMENTS
  error listing the code and the fix; nothing is queued. No contract (or an
  unparseable one) = exactly the pre-contract behavior.
- Approximations (honest): hx-swap association is line-based; (c) requires
  the component name AND `hx-swap-oob` plus the OOB id to appear in the
  proposal; (e) only runs when the contract declares `actions`; `.go` gating
  uses content markers.
- Verified live 2026-09-14 on a /tmp fixture (no volleyball access): valid
  contract accepted; malformed contract refused; the bad templ produced
  R3a/R3b/R3c/R3d with nothing queued; the clean templ queued; identical
  defects without a contract queued (fail-open).
